title: Minimum viable interview panel and escalation matrix
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, portable guide to stand up a minimum viable interview panel (MVIP) for fast hires and to define a clear escalation matrix for candidate adjudication and onboarding handoff. Designed for People Ops and hiring managers who need a fast, low-friction process that still preserves signal quality and bias mitigation.

When to use the MVIP:
- Fast role needs (time-to-offer target <= 10 business days)
- Backfills with clear competency maps
- Small teams where a full cross-functional panel would delay hiring
- Roles with low regulatory risk / non-sensitive data access (use full panel for high-compliance roles)

High-level constraints (keep in mind):
- MV panel must still include technical or functional signal + culture fit + manager decision-maker.
- Default panel size: 3 interviewers (see templates below).
- Use standardized rubric and forced-choice guidance. No free-form pass/fail alone.
- Document decisions in the candidate evidence doc (linked artifact).

Panel templates (pick one by role seniority):
- IC (junior-mid):
  1) Hiring manager (30m) — functional fit, team expectations, plus red flags
  2) Peer engineer (30m) — hands-on/skills probe or work sample review
  3) People Ops structured interview (20m) — culture, career intent, compensation alignment
- IC (senior/staff):
  1) Hiring manager (40m) — strategic scope, outcome expectations
  2) Cross-functional stakeholder (30m) — product/infra/ops as relevant
  3) Technical deep-dive (40m) — architecture/leadership or system design
- Manager hire:
  1) Hiring manager (skip if this is promotion; instead use a peer exec) (40m)
  2) Cross-functional partner (30m)
  3) People Ops management interview (40m) — people strategy, hiring plan, performance mgmt

Rubric (frame and scoring):
- Use 1–4 scale per dimension (1 = insufficient, 2 = developing, 3 = competent, 4 = strong).
- Dimensions (always present): Core competency, Problem solving, Communication, Role ownership, Cultural alignment.
- Minimum thresholds: candidate must score at least two 3s and no 1s across the panel to be considered for offer without escalation.

Sample rubric template (text-ready):
- Core competency: [1–4]  Notes: ____
- Problem solving / approach: [1–4]  Notes: ____
- Communication & clarity: [1–4]  Notes: ____
- Role ownership & initiative: [1–4]  Notes: ____
- Cultural alignment (values-based): [1–4]  Notes: ____
- Overall recommendation (Hire / No hire / Needs escalation) -> reason short: ____

Escalation triggers (when to push to escalation panel / hiring director):
1) Any single 1 in Core competency or Problem solving for roles where these are critical.
2) Conflicting panel signals (one strong hire, one strong no-hire).
3) Compensation or relocation exceptions beyond standard bands.
4) Candidate needs legal or compliance exemptions (background, visa, data access).
5) Manager requests time or evidence to re-interview.

Escalation matrix (roles & SLA):
- Level 1: Hiring Manager + People Ops lead (SLA: 48 business hours) — clarify evidence, quick redo interview, or agree to offer/no-offer.
- Level 2: Hiring Director + People Ops Sr. Partner + Eng/Prod Tech Lead (SLA: 72 business hours) — invoked for cross-team impact, budget/level changes, or compliance concerns.
- Level 3: VP People Ops + Head of Org + Legal (SLA: 5 business days) — invoked rarely: policy/contract exceptions, unusual comp, high-risk hires.

Decisioning flow (quick):
1) Panel completes rubric and posts evidence in candidate doc within 24h.
2) If no escalation triggers and thresholds met -> hiring manager prepares offer packet, People Ops confirms band and drafts LOI.
3) If escalation trigger -> submit to Level 1 with short evidence summary + recommendation.
4) Level 1 either resolves or elevates to Level 2 with documented rationale.

Onboarding handoff (Day 0 — Day 14 compact checklist):
Pre-offer (People Ops):
- Reserve laptop and primary tools (okta, google, github) (owner: IT ops)
- Prepare offer template, confirm manager sign-off on role scope (owner: People Ops + Hiring Mgr)
Day 0 (first day):
- Welcome note + Slack channel created (owner: Hiring manager)
- IT access validated, email + calendar invites (owner: IT ops)
- Buddy assigned and first-meeting scheduled (owner: Hiring manager)
- 1-pager role charter and priorities for first 30/60/90 shared (owner: Hiring manager / peer)
Day 1–3:
- Manager 30-min sync daily (first 3 days) — expectations, quick wins, required access check
- Buddy onboarding sessions: codebase tour or product walkthrough (2 sessions)
- Benefits & payroll enrollment checklist completed (People Ops)
Day 4–10:
- Role-specific ramp tasks assigned (small, measurable deliverables) — track in task board
- Cross-team introductions (engineering, product, infra, security as relevant)
- Technical environment: local dev environment + test harness validated (owner: team)
Day 11–14:
- First feedback checkpoint (manager + new hire) — documented in onboarding doc
- Competency quick eval (mini work sample) if role requires (optional; use if signal low)

Quick templates (copy/paste):
- Offer summary one-liner: "We propose X base + Y equity + Z start date. Team priorities: A, B, C. Compensation band: _____"
- Evidence summary for escalation: "Candidate: [name] Role: [role]. Panel summary: scores: [MGR:3, Peer:4, PO:3]. Trigger: conflicting signal on problem solving. Recommendation: hire + redo deep-probe with Tech Lead (30m)."

Bias-mitigation notes and guardrails (practical):
- Always use the rubric; write 2–3 behavioral examples to justify each score.
- People Ops interviewer must check for pattern of restrictive language in notes before Level 2 escalate.
- If panels include external contractors, mark as non-decision makers.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Create a shortened tech live-coding template for 30m peer probes (Priya to draft) — LOE 2 days.
- Add standardized compensation override form to the Level 1 packet (Omar to own).
- Decide if certain compliance roles should bypass MVIP entirely (legal to advise: Tier list).

Appendix: Compact example (realistic run):
- Role: Backend Engineer (mid)
- Timeline: Requisition approved 11/01, panel scheduled 11/05–11/07, offer 11/10 (9 business days total)
- Panel composition used: Hiring manager, peer engineer, people ops interviewer
- Rubric: all 3 scored >=3, no 1s -> Offer extended; pre-onboard checklist completed before start date.

Document history:
- v0.1 initial draft 2025-11-06 (Maya)
- v0.2 added escalation SLA and onboarding checklist 2026-01-14 (Priya)
- v0.3 draft for review 2026-02-20 (Maya)

Notes for reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; do not expand panel size by default. Use full panel playbook for senior/high-risk roles.
- Please comment in-line in the Confluence canonical page and link back here for final merge.
